sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface localisation confirmed by impermeable fluorescent-ligand staining (CA-Alexa488 / BG-Alexa488; L7). Halo-ACVR1.R206H-HiBiT (same N-terminal Halo junction) displayed expected neoresponsiveness to Activin A and hyperresponsiveness to BMP7 in Acvr1-/- mESCs, demonstrating preserved receptor function (L9).
sites.rationale: L5 and L6 explicitly state that hALK2 (ACVR1) Halo/SNAP fusions are placed 'downstream the signal peptide sequence', which by the authoritative landmarks means after residue 20 (the last signal-peptide residue, S) and before residue 21 (M, the mature N-terminus). Python confirms seq[19]='S' and seq[20]='M'. The extracellular span (21–125, 105 residues) is ample for a ~20 aa tag plus linkers, and the junction is 105 residues from the TM boundary (126), well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. L9 independently validates surface display and full BMP/Activin signalling function of a construct carrying the identical N-terminal Halo junction. Full-length hALK2 (ACVR1) and hALK2-R206H were N-terminally fused with Halo- or SNAP-tags separated by a 5x glycine linker explicitly placed downstream of the signal peptide sequence (residues 1–20) in pcDNA3.1 expression vectors and transfected into mammalian cells. Surface display was confirmed by impermeable CA-Alexa488 / BG-Alexa488 staining (L7). An independent construct (Halo-ACVR1-HiBiT, L8) places the same Halo tag N-terminally and was validated for surface localisation and preserved signalling (L9). ED-epitope-tagged ALK2 (myc or HA, L3/L11) in COS7 cells is consistent with the same junction: ACVR1 is a single-pass type I receptor whose only extracellular region is residues 21–125, so an extracellular-domain tag can only sit at this terminus.

sources.claim: For the generation of the N-terminally Halo- and SNAP-tagged BMP/TGFβ receptor library, hALK1-hALK6, rALK7,hALK2-R206H as well as mAlk1 and zAlk1 were subcloned into pcDNA3.1 mUnc5b-SNAP/Halo and hACVR2A, hACVR2B, hTGFBR2 were subcloned into pcDNA3.1 hBMPR2-LF-SNAP/Halo in between EcoRI and NotI thereby replacing the respective receptor ORF.

literature_notes: L3 and L11 describe ALK2/ACVR1 carrying an 'ED epitope tag (myc or HA)' in COS7 cells but name no specific residue or junction. Because ACVR1 is a single-pass type I receptor with exactly one extracellular region (residues 21–125) and no extracellular C-terminus, topology_derived reasoning places any extracellular-domain tag at the same insert_after_residue=20 junction already validated by L5/L6. These lines therefore corroborate the single site rather than defining a second one. L8 (Halo-ACVR1-HiBiT) names both an N-terminal Halo and a C-terminal HiBiT; the N-terminal Halo maps to the same surface site (insert_after_residue=20), while the C-terminal HiBiT is intracellular and is recorded in other_positions. L10 (zebrafish acvr1l-HA, C-terminal) is an ortholog with an intracellular C-terminal tag and is also recorded in other_positions. No ledger line supports an internal extracellular-loop insertion for ACVR1.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal HA tag inserted at the 3′ end of the full-length hACVR1 coding sequence; the C-terminus (residue 509, C) lies within the intracellular kinase domain (residues 147–509) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
C-terminal HiBiT tag on Halo-ACVR1-HiBiT; same intracellular C-terminus (residue 509, C); not a surface-accessible site.
